subject: Why this warning message about a variable being out of bounds?

messages.author: 706a0969d0cf5307
messages.subject: Why this warning message about a variable being out of bounds?
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to Bayesian things and STAN, so please don't kill me.

I used the attached R code to obtain summaries on posterior distributions for parameters in the attached stan file (a simple model with only 3 levels). A call to stan() yielded a warning of the following type, 36 times in 1000 samples and again 39 times in 1000 samples:

# Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
# stan::prob::beta_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is 4.23105:0, but must be less than or equal to 1
# If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
# but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

I don't actually know why this warning is occurring. I guess it has something to do with the parameter p1 being drawn near 1 some of the time, which somehow leads to the parameter p1tilde being drawn to be out of bounds [0,1]? Does it have something to do with underflow or overflow when a computer stores numbers? 

I'm getting the underflow/overflow idea from the STAN reference manual, which mentions "arithmetic stability" in what it says about informational messages: 

"In cases where the message persists, it is worth investigating the arithmetic stability of the Stan program. There are several tips in this manual and in the user group about how to rewrite problematic programs."


Thanks!
Qian

P.S. I'll read Chapters 10 and 11 of BDA so I actually know what is going on under the hood, if that has anything to do with this warning.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Why this warning message about a variable being out of bounds?
parts:
The problem is that you declare

real<lower=0> p1tilde[J];

which allows any value for p1tilde > 0, and then have
a model statement:

p1tilde[j] ~ beta(10*p1, 10*(1-p1));

which requires p1tilde[j] < 1. So what you want is:

real<lower=0, upper=1> p1tilde[J];

So what Stan does is jump outside of (0,1), then rejects
with an error.

You also want to vectorize, and rewrite as:

ptilde ~ beta(10 * pi, 10 * (1 - pi));

and

a ~ binomial(n, p1tilde);

It'll run a lot faster. But you can probably just reformulate
using the beta-binomial and cut out estimating that p1tilde
altogether:

a ~ beta_binomial(n, 10 * p1, 10 * (1 - p1))

I'm also not sure why you're pegging the prior count to 8 (the parameters
add 1 to the prior counts), but the above should give you much more
efficient inference for p1, which is presumably what you care about.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Why this warning message about a variable being out of bounds?
parts:
The exponential family priors act like data.
So you can think of beta(alpha, beta) as the posterior of
a Bernoulli (or binomial) model starting with a uniform prior
and observing alpha-1 successes and beta-1 failures.
So (alpha + beta - 2) is how many data points the prior is
equivalent to, so your prior beta(10*p1, 10*(1-p1)) with p1 in (0,1)
is defined so that it's equivalent to 8 prior observations.

- Bob
